```artifact
Feature: Alarm Management for Ventilator GUI

  Scenario: LOW VTE alarm is of medium priority
    Given the GUI is initialized
    When a LOW VTE alarm condition is met
    Then the alarm priority displayed should be "Medium"

  Scenario: HIGH VTE alarm is of medium priority
    Given the GUI is initialized
    When a HIGH VTE alarm condition is met
    Then the alarm priority displayed should be "Medium"

  Scenario: Compute HIGH VTE alarm based on VTE threshold
    Given the current breath VTE is 120
    And the HIGH VTE threshold is 100
    When the GUI computes the VTE alarm
    Then a HIGH VTE alarm should be active

  Scenario: Compute VTE for each breath
    Given a series of breath data with varying VTE values
    When the GUI computes VTE for each breath
    Then the computed VTE values should match the input data

  Scenario: Cancel "pressure high" alarm and prevent re-trigger for 2 minutes
    Given a "pressure high" alarm is active
    When the alarm is cancelled
    And 1 minute later the pressure condition remains unchanged
    Then the "pressure high" alarm should not re-trigger
    And after 2 minutes the alarm should remain inactive

  Scenario: Compute high-priority alarm on O2 input line disconnection
    Given the O2 input line is disconnected
    When the GUI computes the alarm status
    Then a high-priority alarm should be triggered

  Scenario: Display all currently active alarms
    Given multiple alarms (HIGH VTE, LOW VTE, O2 disconnection) are active
    When the GUI displays active alarms
    Then all active alarms should be listed

  Scenario Outline: Event log includes confirmed alarm settings
    Given an alarm setting is confirmed
    When the event log is queried
    Then the confirmed alarm setting should appear in the event log

    Examples:
      | alarm_type      | priority | status      |
      | HIGH VTE        | Medium   | Active      |
      | LOW VTE         | Medium   | Inactive    |
      | O2 Disconnection| High     | Confirmed   |
```
